GitHub Issue:
Post Date: 2014-12-14T19:09:06Z
Current Date: April 4 2025
Title: Can an optional and required field of merged interfaces yield a required field?
Description: I have this case from using the mongoose library, in which my domain object, A, might have a DB _id, but the mongoose.Document always has an _id.
I use type A when not in the mongoose portions of the app, and type ADocument only within those parts that deal directly with mongoose.  Note that mongoose defines Document to contain _id like this:

```
interface Document {
    _id: string;
}
```

I tried to model the A - ADocument relationship like this:

```
interface A {
    _id?: string;
}
interface ADoc extends A, mongoose.Document {   
}
```

but I get this error:
_Interface 'ADoc' cannot simultaneously extend types 'A' and 'Document':
 Named properties '_id' of types 'A' and 'Document' are not identical._

I can get around this error by making _id be either optional in both definitions, or required in both.

I expect that the compiler can infer that _id is now required in ADoc. 
Is the current behavior of issuing an error the correct behavior? 
If so, does it make sense to merge such fields so they become required?
